items.followUp: What is an enzyme-substrate complex, and how does it help an enzyme speed up a reaction?

rubric.why: Activation energy is the minimum energy required to start a chemical reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the minimum energy needed to start a reaction.

rubric.why: Enzymes lower the energy requirement by providing an alternative pathway, often involving an enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.description: Explains how enzymes lower activation energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that an enzyme provides an alternative pathway or forms an enzyme-substrate complex that requires less activation energy.

modelAnswer: Activation energy is the minimum energy required to start a chemical reaction.
An enzyme forms an enzyme-substrate complex and provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation-energy requirement.

items.followUp: What is a coenzyme? Give one example.

rubric.why: Cofactors are non-protein substances needed for the activity of some enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cofactors are non-protein substances required for enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Metal ions, coenzymes and prosthetic groups are types of cofactors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one correct type of cofactor.

modelAnswer: Cofactors are non-protein substances required by some enzymes for their activity.
They include metal ions, coenzymes and prosthetic groups.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of a chloroplast and explain its role in photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Plastids are double-membraned organelles found in plant cells.
rubric.description: States the general features of plastids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying plastids as plant-cell organelles with a double membrane.

rubric.why: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking chlorophyll-containing chloroplasts with photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromoplasts contain pigments or give colour to plant parts.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that leucoplasts are colourless or store food.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts can store food materials such as starch, oils and proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one substance stored by leucoplasts.

modelAnswer: Plastids are double-membraned organelles found in plant cells.
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments that give colour to flowers and fruits.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
Leucoplasts may store starch, oils or proteins.
